Design system — stylesheets, colours and UI rules

The rulebook for anyone who builds or customises SATOM's interface — which stylesheet owns what, every colour token and status badge with its measured contrast, the components to reuse, card grids, charts, the CSP constraints and how plugin views inherit the look.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereServer side — app/static/css/ (fortiweb.css and the feature stylesheets); the theme editor is Settings → User Interface → Appearance
On this page
  • 1. SATOM is a light product
  • 2. Stylesheets — what each file owns
  • 3. Tokens
  • Colour tokens (SATOM Aurora)

  • 4. Status colours — the badge set

Appearance explains the mechanism: design tokens, named themes, the value allowlist, the contrast audit and how to get back. This document is the rulebook for anyone who writes a template, a stylesheet, a chart or a plugin view: which files own which styles, which colours exist, which components to reuse, and which mistakes have already shipped once.

When a rule here changes, this file changes in the same commit. The values quoted below are the stylesheet defaults (the built-in theme SATOM Aurora); app/static/css/fortiweb.css is the source and wins over this page.

1. SATOM is a light product#

There is one canvas and it is light. There is no dark mode: no prefers-color-scheme, no data-theme, no body class. A dark canvas is not offered as a theme either, because the status tints are still literal colours (Appearance).

Two things follow, and both have shipped by mistake before:

  • Dark glassmorphism is a grey slab here. A card painted rgba(30,41,59,.8) with a backdrop-filter on a white page renders as an opaque grey block.
  • Dark-theme pastels are unreadable here. Status pills in #6ee7b7, #fcd34d or #fca5a5 on a 12 % tint of their own hue measure about 1.4:1 — a crit badge nobody can read.

The only dark surfaces in the product are the navigation chrome (sidebar and top bar) and code (.fw-code-block, the Web Server Manager editor, a template's source in a viewer). Modals, drawers, pickers and empty states are light — the audit detail drawer, the device switcher, the baseline template viewer and the High Availability node cards were dark until 4.12 and were converted.

Map canvases are light too. The Service Diagram fleet map (static/js/fleet_map.js, templates/architecture/index.html) and Network Architecture (templates/netarch/index.html, static/js/netarch.js) drew on a dark "neon" canvas until 4.12. They now draw on #F8FAFE with a faint grid: white nodes with a soft shadow, theme text colours, and the 600/700 hues listed in §3 for lines, states and zones.

2. Stylesheets — what each file owns#

File Owns
fortiweb.css The base theme: every --fw-* token, layout (sidebar, top bar, content), cards, tables, forms, buttons, badges, alerts. Loaded on every page.
analytics.css Analytics boards and period reports.
waf.css The WAF fleet pages (findings, pills, borrowed settings).
wiki.css Operations › Wiki (two-column layout by container query).
wsm.css Web Server Manager (Linux ADOM): layout only, on SATOM's own components.
apps_portal.css The Apps-only portal: the console's light theme and top bar without the sidebar.
app_design.css Plugin Studio app designer: spacing and structure only; colours come from tokens, overridable inside .sapp alone.
example_browser.css The shared Studio example browser (self-contained light theme).
icon_picker.css The icon picker used by Plugin Studio and Report Studio.
plugin-kit.css Base look of every plugin view and widget; inlined into the sandboxed frame (§9).

Rules:

  • A self-contained page family gets its own file, not an append to fortiweb.css. fortiweb.css is the file every feature edits, so appending to it is how two concurrent changes collide.
  • A feature stylesheet lays out SATOM's components; it does not restyle them. Colours come from tokens (§3) and statuses from the badge set (§4).
  • Stylesheets are served through asset() with an mtime cache-buster: a static-only change needs no restart.
  • Every third-party browser asset is vendored under app/static/vendor/ and listed in vendor/MANIFEST.json with its hash: Bootstrap 5.3.3, Bootstrap Icons 1.11.3, Inter 4.1, Chart.js 4.4.4, Toast UI Editor 3.2.2. Nothing loads from another origin, so an offline node on an isolated management network renders exactly like an online one (tests/test_offline_assets.py; procedure in docs/engineering.md §9.1).

3. Tokens#

Every colour, radius and shadow that a theme can change is a --fw-* custom property in :root of fortiweb.css. The theme editor's registry is generated from it (deploy/gen_theme_tokens.py), so a new token is two edits in one commit — see Appearance.

Colour tokens (SATOM Aurora)#

Token Value Used for Contrast
--fw-content-bg #F3F6FC Page canvas —
--fw-surface #FFFFFF Cards, inputs, tables, modals —
--fw-surface-alt #F8FAFE Muted surface (striping, wells) —
--fw-border #DCE4F3 Card and control borders —
--fw-border-light #EAEFF9 Dividers —
--fw-text-primary #0C1B33 Body text 15.9:1 on canvas
--fw-text-secondary #51607F Secondary text 6.3:1 on white
--fw-accent #0A3F9F Links, primary actions, focus 9.4:1 on white
--fw-accent-hover #041F5A Hover / pressed accent —
--fw-accent-light rgba(10,63,159,.10) Selected-row tint —
--fw-sidebar-bg #0A3F9F Navigation background —
--fw-sidebar-text #C7D6F5 Navigation text 6.5:1 on sidebar
--fw-sidebar-section #9FB6E0 Section captions 4.6:1 on sidebar
--fw-sidebar-active #F3B52F Active marker 5.2:1 on sidebar
--fw-topbar-bg #041F5A Top bar —
--fw-success / --fw-danger / --fw-warning / --fw-info #28A745 / #DC3545 / #F3B52F / #17A2B8 Fills and icons — not text on white (use §4) —

Brand tokens: --fw-gradient-brand (blue ramp `#041F5A → #0A3F9F → #12B8FF →

39D4FF),--fw-gradient-accent(gold ramp#C98A11 → #F3B52F → #FFD45A`),#

--fw-glow, --fw-glow-accent, --fw-glow-strength. A gradient is paint, not a colour: only background-image or border-image (Appearance).

Layout tokens: --fw-sidebar-width 264 px, --fw-topbar-height 50 px, --fw-radius 4 px, --fw-radius-lg 8 px, --fw-card-shadow, --fw-card-shadow-hover, --fw-transition 0.2 s, --fw-font (Inter, then the system stack).

Rules for tokens#

  • Use the token, never its value. A literal #0A3F9F in a feature stylesheet does not follow the active theme.
  • A fallback inside var() must be the current default, or absent. A stale fallback is a second palette hiding in the code (the pre-1.2.3 accent #EF5424 survived this way in several rules).
  • Drawings read the token too. An SVG presentation attribute (fill="…", stroke="…") cannot hold var(): put the colour in style instead (style="stroke:var(--fw-accent, #0A3F9F)"). Canvas and Chart.js code reads it at run time: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--fw-accent').trim() || '#0A3F9F'.
  • Categorical palettes are not the accent. A palette that tells categories apart (ER diagram domains, map zones, chart series after the first) keeps its own fixed hues; only the colour that means "the accent" (selection, focus, highlight, the first series) comes from the token.
  • Never set fill on #id text. In an SVG, a rule like #mapSvg text { fill: … } outranks every .class rule and every fill attribute set from JavaScript, so per-class text colours silently stop working. Put the default on the <svg> (#mapSvg { fill: … }) and let text inherit it; class rules and attributes then win as intended.

Colours on a light canvas (lines, states, categories)#

The bright "500" hues of dark dashboards fall to 2–3:1 on white. On a SATOM canvas use the 600/700 step of the same hue:

Meaning Use Instead of
Default line / HTTP / selection #1D4ED8 #4f8cff, #3b82f6
OK, HTTPS, protected #15803D (text #15692A) #22c55e, #10b981
Warning, monitor mode #B45309 #f59e0b
Down, denied, error #B91C1C #ef4444
Pool / segment (violet) #7C3AED #8b5cf6, #a78bfa
Back-end (teal) #0F766E #14b8a6
Off / disabled #64748B —

Zone palette (white text on the pill, ≥4.5:1): `#1D4ED8 #7C3AED #0E7490

047857 #B45309 #B91C1C #BE185D #0F766E #7E22CE #4D7C0F #C2410C #4338CA#

0369A1 #15803D #A16207 #BE123C— the same list infleet_map.js` and the#

device picker, so a zone keeps its colour everywhere. - Contrast floor: 4.5:1 for text (WCAG 2.1 AA). The theme editor warns under 4.5:1 and refuses under 3.0:1 without "apply anyway"; tests/test_theme.py fails if the shipped palette drops a text pair under AA.

Built-in themes#

Theme What it is
SATOM Aurora The shipped look. Carries no overrides: it is the stylesheet.
SATOM Classic The palette before 1.2.3 (orange accent #EF5424, 3.52:1 on white).
SATOM Slate, SATOM Graphite Alternate light palettes, AA-clean.

Built-ins cannot be edited or deleted; they are the way back (Appearance).

4. Status colours — the badge set#

Status is shown with .fw-badge-* and nothing else. The set is calibrated against white (the final block in fortiweb.css):

Class Text Tint Text contrast on white
.fw-badge-success #15692A rgba(40,167,69,.16) 6.8:1
.fw-badge-warning #7A5700 rgba(255,193,7,.20) 6.6:1
.fw-badge-danger #8B1C2A rgba(220,53,69,.16) 9.1:1
.fw-badge-info #0A5F6C rgba(23,162,184,.16) 7.3:1
.fw-badge-secondary #3D4550 rgba(108,117,125,.16) 9.7:1
.fw-badge-primary --fw-accent-hover 16 % of --fw-accent follows the theme
  • Add .fw-badge-nowrap when a two-word verdict sits in a narrow column: a pill is drawn around one line.
  • The WAF pages use one extra hue, purple #4C2A85 (waf.css), for informational findings and borrowed settings.
  • Never invent a status colour. A new state maps to one of the classes above.

5. Components#

Reuse before writing CSS:

Need Use
A panel .fw-card (surface, border, --fw-radius-lg, card shadow)
Buttons Bootstrap .btn with .btn-fw-* / .btn-fw-secondary. Button labels never wrap.
Messages .fw-alert-*
Status .fw-badge-* (§4)
Navigation in a page .fw-breadcrumb, .nav-tabs
Code, CLI output .fw-code-block (the one dark surface)
Icons Bootstrap Icons (bi bi-*)
  • Typeface: Inter (vendored variable font) through --fw-font.
  • Appliances show the hostname only in lists and combos; address, port and classification go in the tooltip.
  • Every interface string is English and wrapped for translation (_()); the console is translated with Babel (de/es/fr/it), default English.

6. Card grids: collapsed by default, dense mosaic#

Pages that list one card per appliance or probe (Monitoring probes, Service Monitor) follow one pattern, implemented in app/templates/monitoring/_probe_page.html:

  • Collapsed by default. With a hundred appliances, "everything collapsed" is the only usable default.
  • The browser stores the OPEN set, not the closed one (localStorage key satom.probecards.open.<page>). An empty set means all collapsed, with no first-run flag. Never reuse an older key with the opposite meaning: it would expand exactly the cards the operator closed.
  • Grid: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(258px, 1fr)) with grid-auto-flow: row dense. An expanded card spans the row (grid-column: 1 / -1): a tall item in a narrow column stretches every tile beside it.
  • Collapsed is not hidden: the header keeps the status badge and a summary chip (for example avg Mbps · N pol) on one line.

7. Charts#

Chart.js 4.4.4, vendored.

  • Grid lines must be visible on white. A 7 % slate grid is invisible in a white modal; use about 8 % (rgba(31,41,51,.08)) or a solid #E3E8F0.
  • Series colours come from tokens or the badge set, never pastels.
  • A failed query is drawn as an ERROR, never as an empty chart. The same holds for a collector that failed: absence of data is not health.

8. What the Content-Security-Policy does to markup#

The console enforces a nonce-based CSP. It shapes how UI is written:

  • No on*= handler attributes, anywhere, including markup built by JavaScript. Use addEventListener with data-* hooks and delegation.
  • Every inline <script> and <style> carries the page nonce.
  • style="…" attributes are allowed, but a class is preferred.
  • Dynamic UI is built with createElement, not HTML strings with handlers.
  • A web font or stylesheet from another origin is blocked — another reason everything is vendored (§2).

Details and the Turbo nonce re-stamp: docs/engineering.md §9.

9. Plugin and app views#

Plugin views (Report Studio views and widgets, Plugin Studio app views) render in a sandboxed iframe that cannot load fortiweb.css. The frame therefore carries the look itself: every --fw-* token at its default, then the active theme's overrides, then plugin-kit.css (inlined), then the plugin's own CSS. A theme change reaches every plugin that uses the tokens or the kit.

  • The frame sandbox is allow-scripts allow-modals allow-forms; form-action 'none' keeps a form from leaving the frame. Without allow-forms the browser blocks the submit before the bridge sees it (tests/test_studio_view.py pins it).
  • A plugin view is proven in a real browser, not by the server render: the server render cannot exercise the parent/frame bridge.
  • What a plugin stylesheet may contain: user guide, Report Studio, Plugin CSS rules.

10. Checklist for a UI change#

  1. Panels are .fw-card, statuses are .fw-badge-*, colours are var(--fw-*).
  2. No dark surface other than code; no pastels; no glassmorphism.
  3. Text contrast measured at 4.5:1 or better on the surface it sits on.
  4. New page family → its own stylesheet; new third-party asset → vendored and listed in MANIFEST.json.
  5. No on*= attributes; inline blocks carry the nonce.
  6. English strings, wrapped for translation.
  7. Charts: visible grid, error state for a failed query.
  8. Card grids: collapsed by default, open set stored, expanded card spans the row.
  9. A plugin view is checked in a browser.

11. Where it is enforced#

Test Holds
tests/test_theme.py Token registry matches the stylesheet; shipped palette AA-clean; built-ins state their own gradients; no gradient fed to a colour-only property
tests/test_offline_assets.py Every browser asset is vendored and hashed
tests/test_studio_view.py Plugin frame sandbox and CSP
